2.title: Foam-Agent opening frame
bullets: Start with the pain point: CFD workflows still rely on expert handoffs.
Name retrieval, file generation, and error correction as the three automation moves.
Land on the practical outcome: more engineers can run simulations from plain language.

3.title: ReAct method setup
bullets: Explain that reasoning traces and external actions are interleaved in one prompting loop.
Use the Wikipedia example to make the action channel concrete for the audience.
Bridge to the next slide by saying the core idea survives even when the example is simplified.

5.title: MAST failure taxonomy emphasis
bullets: Frame this slide as a cautionary lens for multi-agent demos that look polished but break in deployment.
Call out the LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline as the reusable evaluation asset.
End with the open-sourced dataset as the reason this paper matters beyond taxonomy labels.

6.title: MultiAgentBench closing beat
bullets: Position this benchmark as the evaluation counterpart to the workflow systems shown earlier.
Mention both collaboration and competition so the scope sounds broader than a single benchmark track.
Close the rehearsal section by pointing the audience to the released code and data.
